headline: 3.5 lakh people marooned by flash floods in southern Chattogram
summary: Torrential rains and hill torrents have crippled communication and caused Tk 39 crore in losses, with Satkania upazila being the worst hit.
details: Flash floods triggered by four days of heavy downpours and upstream hill torrents have left thousands marooned and crippled regional communication in southern Chattogram.
The crisis is most severe in Satkania upazila, where approximately 3.5 lakh residents are trapped as 70 to 80 percent of the locality is submerged.
Overflowing Sangu and Dolu rivers breached embankments, inundating critical infrastructure including the Satkania Upazila Health Complex, local courts, and the police station.
Agricultural losses are extensive, with 6,591 hectares of Aus rice and 4,167 hectares of summer vegetables destroyed, alongside 565 hectares of Aman seedbeds.
Monsoon floods have caused an estimated loss of Tk 39 crore, with over 7,400 ponds, shrimp farms, and water bodies submerged across Patiya, Anwara, and Banshkhali.
Regional logistics have been paralyzed, with the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar Highway submerged at Hashimpur and the Keranihat-Bandarban road cut off.
The district administration has activated over 230 emergency shelters, including 110 in Banshkhali and 89 in Satkania, while cancelling all official leaves.
While floodwaters have begun to recede in parts of coastal Banshkhali, communication to many unions remains severed, leaving thousands still waiting for relief.
caption:
3.5 lakh people are trapped in southern Chattogram as flash floods submerge 80% of some areas.

Flash floods triggered by four days of heavy downpours and upstream hill torrents have left thousands marooned and crippled regional communication in southern Chattogram.

The crisis is most severe in Satkania upazila, where approximately 3.5 lakh residents are trapped as 70 to 80 percent of the locality is submerged.

Overflowing Sangu and Dolu rivers breached embankments, inundating critical infrastructure including the Satkania Upazila Health Complex, local courts, and the police station.

Agricultural losses are extensive, with 6,591 hectares of Aus rice and 4,167 hectares of summer vegetables destroyed, alongside 565 hectares of Aman seedbeds.

Monsoon floods have caused an estimated loss of Tk 39 crore, with over 7,400 ponds, shrimp farms, and water bodies submerged across Patiya, Anwara, and Banshkhali.

Regional logistics have been paralyzed, with the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar Highway submerged at Hashimpur and the Keranihat-Bandarban road cut off.

The district administration has activated over 230 emergency shelters, including 110 in Banshkhali and 89 in Satkania, while cancelling all official leaves.

While floodwaters have begun to recede in parts of coastal Banshkhali, communication to many unions remains severed, leaving thousands still waiting for relief.

headline: Official suspended after primary scholarship results leaked for 9 districts
summary: The Directorate of Primary Education has launched a probe after results for students in the Dhaka division were uploaded to the web portal before the official announcement.
details: The results of the primary scholarship examination for class five students were leaked before their official publication on Thursday. Results for nine districts under the Dhaka division were uploaded to designated links and shared on social media before the formal announcement.
Following the incident, the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE) has requested action against an official allegedly involved and formed a three-member probe committee to investigate the breach.
DPE Assistant Maintenance Md Mehtab Kayes was assigned to prepare the links for the web portal but was explicitly instructed not to upload the results before official approval.
The DPE stated that required security protocols were not followed while creating the links and uploading the results to the live server around 10:00 am on Thursday.
This year, 82,500 students will receive scholarships, with 80 percent coming from government primary schools and 20 percent from private schools and kindergartens.
Nearly 6.5 lakh students took part in the examination, which was held between April 15 and 20 across all districts, including a special schedule for the hill districts.
caption:
Results for 9 districts leaked before official announcement. An official has been suspended as a probe begins.

The results of the primary scholarship examination for class five students were leaked before their official publication on Thursday. Results for nine districts under the Dhaka division were uploaded to designated links and shared on social media before the formal announcement.

Following the incident, the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE) has requested action against an official allegedly involved and formed a three-member probe committee to investigate the breach.

DPE Assistant Maintenance Md Mehtab Kayes was assigned to prepare the links for the web portal but was explicitly instructed not to upload the results before official approval.

The DPE stated that required security protocols were not followed while creating the links and uploading the results to the live server around 10:00 am on Thursday.

This year, 82,500 students will receive scholarships, with 80 percent coming from government primary schools and 20 percent from private schools and kindergartens.

Nearly 6.5 lakh students took part in the examination, which was held between April 15 and 20 across all districts, including a special schedule for the hill districts.
